summary: 1927 steel fire tower in Indian Trail Conservation Area, Dent County, Missouri; sources give heights from 72 to 90 feet; NHLR-registered 2013; access today unconfirmed.

facts.design: Steel fire tower with a 7-by-7-foot steel cab

access.note: The conservation area is open to the public under department rules. No source read confirms that the tower itself is open to climb today.

visit.trail_note: From Salem, Highway 19 northeast 12 miles reaches the area. A 2019 Missouri Conservationist article describes visitors seeing the view from atop the lookout tower.

events.note: Completed by September 1927 per a Game and Fish Department clipping; the register gives 1927
Towerman on duty through the fire season, per a December 1935 clipping
Water system installed at the tower site, fiscal 1958-59 report
Three-bedroom residence built at the tower site, with a new parking lot and entrance road to the tower, fiscal 1973-74 report

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register calls Indian Trail the second lookout in Missouri. The 1927 clipping only says it was the second tower of its kind erected by the Game and Fish Department, after Deer Run State Park. The two claims differ in scope, and the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Height is unresolved. Sources give 90 ft (Aug 1927, under construction), 73 ft to the deck plus a 9 ft steel room (Sept 1927), 72 ft (Apr 1928), 80 ft (Dec 1935) and 85 ft (1939-41 annual report and NHLR). The record's height_m 25.9 equals 85 ft and is kept as the NHLR and annual-report figure. The guide's cab-floor measure is closest to the September 1927 figure of 73 ft to the deck (about 22.3 m), so the editor should decide which measure the record carries. Built 1927 is supported by NHLR and by the September 1927 completion clipping. Status 'standing' rests on the NHLR description, which is undated. Access level 'public' refers to the conservation area; no source read confirms the tower is open to climb today, and the 2019 article is the latest visitor description read. Staffing 'seasonal' rests on the 1935 clipping alone. The 2019 Conservationist article gives the area as 13,005 acres; the MDC page gives 13,503, which the story uses. The nature.mdc.mo.gov page returned 404 and was not used. No photos added; the record's existing NHLR photo is unchanged.
